key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines welding simulation and Gaussian-process surrogates to screen in-space joining conditions and control strategies before physical testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could help robotic welding systems adjust power as travel speed changes, supporting more consistent weld geometry.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict weld responses.
Simulated six-axis robot uses proportional power-setting control along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network across eight outputs; finite-volume checks placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation are still needed.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
